item.title: Trump says Iran deal 'largely negotiated,' Strait of Hormuz to reopen
item.description: President Donald Trump declared Saturday that a memorandum of understanding with Iran has been "largely negotiated," with final details to be announced shortly, marking the most concrete step yet toward ending months of conflict between the two nations.

item.title: Iran agreed to give up enriched uranium in US deal, officials say
item.description: Two US officials told the New York Times that Iran has agreed in broad terms to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium as part of a framework deal announced by President Donald Trump, who declared Saturday that a peace agreement had been "largely negotiated." But a senior Iranian source subsequently told Reuters that Tehran has not agreed to hand over its enriched uranium, highlighting the persistent contradictions between American and Iranian accounts of the deal's terms.

item.title: Iran says US deal 'not imminent' as both sides temper expectations
item.description:
Efforts to finalize a peace agreement between the United States and Iran slowed on Monday as both sides tempered expectations, with Iran's foreign ministry declaring that a deal is "not imminent" even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested an announcement could come "maybe today."

The impasse centers on a proposed memorandum of understanding that would end the three-month-old war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and set the stage for broader negotiations over Iran's nuclear program and sanctions relief. President Trump, posting on Truth Social over the weekend, said the deal "will either be a great and meaningful one, or there will be no deal," while cautioning his team not to "rush into" an agreement.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls to 'disarm' AI in first encyclical
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV on Monday released his first encyclical, a sweeping nearly 43,000-word document that calls for the "disarming" of artificial intelligence and warns that the technology risks becoming a modern Tower of Babel if left unchecked in the hands of powerful corporations and governments.

The encyclical, titled "Magnifica Humanitas" ("Magnificent Humanity"), was presented by the American-born pontiff in the Vatican's Synod Hall — a break with tradition, as popes do not typically speak at the launch of their own encyclicals. Joining him on the panel was Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic, the AI safety company currently embroiled in a legal battle with the Trump administration over the military use of its technology.

item.title: Inaudible sounds hidden in podcasts can hijack AI voice assistants, researchers find
item.description: A team of security researchers has shown that imperceptible audio signals hidden in podcasts, YouTube videos, and voice calls can manipulate AI voice assistants into performing unauthorized actions — a finding presented this week at the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy in San Francisco that exposes a new class of vulnerability in the rapidly expanding world of voice-based AI.

item.title: Oil and LNG tankers resume Strait of Hormuz transits after three-month halt
item.description: Multiple vessels carrying crude oil and liquefied natural gas have begun transiting the Strait of Hormuz, offering the clearest sign yet that limited commercial shipping is restarting after nearly three months of disruption caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: Trump urges Arab leaders to normalize Israel ties as Iran deal nears
item.description:
President Donald Trump told the leaders of several Arab and Muslim-majority countries during a phone call on Saturday that he expects them to normalize relations with Israel and join the Abraham Accords once a deal to end the war with Iran is reached, according to Axios. The request was reportedly met with silence from the leaders on the call, the Times of Israel reported.

The call came as Washington and Tehran appeared close to signing a memorandum of understanding to end hostilities, with a senior U.S. official saying the deal could come "in the coming days". Trump declared Saturday that the agreement had been "largely negotiated," though disputes over wording, sanctions relief, frozen assets, and the terms of uranium disposal remain unresolved.

item.title: WHO chief warns Ebola 'outpacing' response as deaths hit 220
item.description:
The World Health Organization's director-general warned on Monday that the Ebola outbreak tearing through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is outrunning international containment efforts, with 220 suspected deaths and cases mounting rapidly across the region.

"We are urgently scaling up operations, but at the moment the epidemic is outpacing us," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, adding that a delay in detecting cases meant responders were now "playing catch-up." He said he would travel to Congo on Tuesday to assess the response firsthand.

The remarks came as Uganda confirmed two additional Ebola cases on Monday, bringing its total to seven confirmed infections. The DRC remains the epicenter of the outbreak, with its health ministry reporting hundreds of suspected cases and deaths concentrated in the conflict-ridden Ituri and North Kivu provinces.

item.title: AI safety filters on Meta, Google models stripped in minutes, FT finds
item.description: Software tools that remove safety protections from AI models developed by Meta and Google can bypass guardrails in a matter of minutes, according to an investigation published by the Financial Times on Sunday. The modified systems responded to prompts involving biological weapons, malware creation, and child exploitation, raising fresh concerns about the adequacy of voluntary safety measures across the AI industry.

item.title: DRC Ebola outbreak tops 900 cases as violence hampers response
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 900 suspected cases, with WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warning that the fast-moving epidemic is outrunning containment efforts. The Congolese government reported 904 suspected cases and 119 suspected fatalities as of Sunday, May 24, while attacks on health facilities have driven patients into communities and complicated an already strained response.

item.title: Russia warns foreigners to leave Kyiv ahead of 'systematic strikes'
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry on Monday urged foreign citizens and diplomats to evacuate Kyiv, declaring that its armed forces would begin "systematic assaults" on military-industrial sites, decision-making centres, and command posts in the Ukrainian capital. The warning came a day after one of the most devastating aerial bombardments to hit Kyiv in months.

item.title: Carney calls Alberta separation vote a 'dangerous bluff,' cites Brexit experience
item.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney warned Monday that Alberta's planned referendum on separation is a "dangerous bluff," cautioning that anyone who believes the results could be used as leverage in future negotiations is courting disaster. Carney drew on his experience as governor of the Bank of England during the 2016 Brexit vote, saying people are still trying to undo the damage caused by that decision a decade later.

The remarks come four days after Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced that an October 19 referendum — already set to include questions on immigration and constitutional reform — will now also ask residents whether the province should remain part of Canada or begin the legal process toward a binding separation vote.

item.title: Lavrov urges Rubio to evacuate US embassy from Kyiv
item.description:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday to urge the evacuation of American diplomats from Kyiv, delivering a warning that Russian forces plan to launch "systematic and consistent strikes" on the Ukrainian capital, including against "decision-making centers" and military-industrial facilities.

The phone call, confirmed by Russia's foreign ministry, came as Moscow issued a broader public warning to all foreign nationals, diplomats, and international organizations to leave Kyiv immediately. There was no immediate comment from the US State Department.

item.title: Iran would reopen Strait of Hormuz 30 days after deal, Nikkei reports
item.description:
Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz approximately 30 days after reaching an agreement with the United States to end hostilities, Japan's Nikkei 225 newspaper reported on Monday, citing a Middle East diplomatic source. Under the reported plan, Iran would clear mines from the strategic waterway during the 30-day post-agreement window, after which ships from all countries would navigate freely, with Tehran also ceasing its collection of transit fees.

The report adds that the ceasefire agreed in early April would be extended for 60 days, during which talks on Iran's nuclear program would be held.

item.title: Iran votes to restore internet after 87-day blackout
item.description: The Iranian government on Monday approved a decision to restore nationwide internet access after a blackout lasting nearly three months, according to the Fars news agency. The vote by the country's Cyberspace Regulation Committee passed with nine members in favor and three opposed, marking a potential turning point in what has become one of the longest government-imposed internet shutdowns ever recorded.

item.title: Netanyahu orders intensified strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday ordered a further escalation of military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, vowing to "crush" the Iran-backed group amid ongoing drone attacks on Israeli positions despite a ceasefire that has been in effect since April.

"I have ordered an even greater acceleration of our operations," Netanyahu said in a video statement posted on his Telegram channel. "We will intensify our blows, increase our firepower, and we will crush them."

The Israeli military responded by launching strikes across the Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon and targeting towns in the south, killing at least three people, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes followed Israeli evacuation orders for 10 villages, with military spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee accusing Hezbollah of breaching the truce.

item.title: Iran says Khamenei suffered only 'superficial' wounds in February airstrikes
item.description: Iran's Health Ministry on Monday publicly detailed for the first time the injuries sustained by Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei during the February 28 US-Israeli strikes on Tehran, describing them as minor and dismissing months of international reports that he had been critically wounded or disfigured.

item.title: US strikes Iranian targets near Hormuz amid fragile peace talks
item.description: The U.S. military launched strikes targeting Iranian missile launch sites and boats near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, describing the action as "self-defense" even as fragile peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran continue.

item.title: Putin signs decree canceling debts for new Ukraine war recruits
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Monday canceling debts of up to 10 million roubles — roughly $140,000 — for new military recruits and their spouses, the Kremlin announced, as Moscow continues to deploy financial incentives to sustain its war effort in Ukraine more than four years after the full-scale invasion began.

item.title: Cuba publishes names of 2,000 pardoned prisoners
item.description: Cuba on Monday disclosed the identities of more than 2,000 prisoners pardoned under a sweeping amnesty first announced in April, publishing their names in the country's official government gazette for the first time since the decree was signed nearly two months ago.
